newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON SQUAD.

text.p: Pen pictures of Wimbledon players ahead of Sunday's F.A. Cup semifinal against Chelsea at Highbury:

Neil Sullivan, goalkeeper, 26. Some outstanding displays this season won this London born-and-bred keeper an international call-up -- for Scotland. Qualifies through his grandparents, but has yet to play for his adopted country. Been at Wimbledon since he was a teenager.

Kenny Cunningham, defender, 25. Republic of Ireland international who joined Wimbledon for 1.3 million pounds ($2.1 million) from Millwall in November 1994. Started at minor Irish club Tolka Rovers and moved to Millwall in 1989.

Alan Kimble, defender, 30. Been playing some of the best football of his career. Previously with Charlton and Cambridge, he moved to Wimbledon in 1993 after making 299 league appearances for Cambridge.

Dean Blackwell, defender, 27. Joined Wimbledon from school and established himself in the team in the 1990-91 season. Missed most of last season through injury but came back to play key role in the club's current success.

Chris Perry, defender, 23. At only 5ft 8ins (1.73m), one of the smallest centre-backs in England. But his pace, perception and tackling have made him one of the best around and his dramatic improvement this season could lead to an England call-up. Another locally-born player who joined Wimbledon from school.
Brian McAllister, defender, 26. Scottish-born defender who has been at Wimbledon since he was a teenager developing through the youth ranks.

Neal Ardley, defender/midfielder, 24. Another locally-born player who developed through Wimbledon's apprentice scheme. A former England Under-21 player with 10 caps, who is most effective wide in midfield.

Peter Fear, midfielder, 23. A defensive midfielder and highly effective man-marker whose nickname is "Rash" as he tends to get all over his opponents. Another player developed by Wimbledon's youth scheme and another former England Under-21 cap.

Vinnie Jones, midfielder, 32. Former hod-carrier, sometime male model, chat show host, occasional Welsh international skipper. Tattooed, crop-haired, hard-tackling member of Wimbledon side that won the F.A. Cup in 1988. Left for Leeds and also played for Sheffield United and Chelsea before returning to the Dons in 1992. Infamous for having been sent off 13 times in his career, but this season has confounded many with some hitherto unseen aspects of his soccer skills. Club captain.

Oyvind Leonhardsen, midfielder/forward, 26. Norwegian international who joined Wimbledon for 700,000 pounds in January 1995 and now rated as one of the most skilful and effective attacking midfielders in England. Played for Molde and Rosenborg. Epitomises Wimbledon's transition from a long-ball side to one which is skilful and attractive.
Jon Goodman, midfielder, 26. Joined Wimbledon in a joint-deal which also brought Kenny Cunningham to the club. Irish international who started his career as a striker but plays deeper for the Dons.

Dean Holdsworth, forward, 26. Twin brother of David Holdsworth of Watford, his form has dipped this season as off-field problems have dominated his life. On his day an effective striker with a good goals/game ratio. Has struggled for a place in the side recently.

Robbie Earle, midfield, 32. Has scored in every round of the F.A. Cup so far and has been having an excellent season. At the age of 32 was put on stand-by for England's World Cup qualifer against Italy in February. Strong physically, his non-stop running style causes opponents plenty of problems.

Efan Ekoku, forward, 29. Nigerian international who was born in Manchester. Joined Wimbledon from Norwich for 920,000 pounds in October 1994 -- and scored his first goal for Wimbledon against Norwich a few days later. Released by Nigeria from World Cup duty to play this weekend.

Marcus Gayle, forward, 26. Lithe, skillful forward who is enjoying his best season since joining Wimbledon from Brentford for a bargain 250,000 pounds in March 1994. A former England youth international.

Andy Clarke, forward, 29. Joined Wimbledon from then non-league Barnet for 150,000 pounds in February 1991, at the time the record transfer fee paid for a semi-professional player. Has now made over 100 appearances for Wimbledon.

Mick Harford, forward, 37. Made his league debut 20 years ago and Wimbledon is his 10th club. Had a spell with Sunday's opponents, Chelsea, in the 1992-93 season and has now made over 700 league appearances. Played twice for England in the 1980s. Has played mainly as substitute this season but is still fit and effective and retirement seems a long way off.

Joe Kinnear, Manager, 50. Born in Dublin, he spent his best years as a player at Tottenham where he formed a great full-back partnership with the late Cyril Knowles. Won the F.A. Cup with Spurs in 1967, the UEFA Cup in 1972 and the League Cup in 1971 and 1973. Injury ended his playing career soon after he joined Brighton in 1975. Capped 26 times by Ireland, he became Wimbledon manager in January 1992.
